title: Local Model Ingress/Egress
summary: Control how requests enter a locally hosted model and how data, tools, telemetry, and updates leave its environment.
overview: Local model ingress and egress define the network and application boundaries around self-hosted inference. Ingress covers client authentication, allowed request sizes, routing, and admission. Egress covers tool calls, artifact downloads, telemetry, remote fallbacks, and any other outbound transfer. Hosting weights locally does not by itself prevent data from leaving the environment.

Network controls and application policy solve different problems. A network rule can restrict destinations but usually cannot decide whether a particular prompt is authorized for a tool. Conversely, an application allow-list is incomplete if a compromised process can reach arbitrary endpoints. Use layered identity, network isolation, controlled proxies, and explicit data-flow ownership.

production.poc: A prototype inventories every inbound and outbound connection, including automatic model downloads and telemetry.
production.production: Production authenticates the model endpoint, denies unnecessary network paths, and routes permitted tools through governed adapters.
production.scale: Enterprise scale manages certificate rotation, offline artifact delivery, regional egress policy, audit retention, and emergency maintenance access without exposing the serving port broadly.

components.name: Ingress gateway
components.role: Authenticates clients, enforces request limits, and routes to approved local models.

components.name: Inference network zone
components.role: Limits direct access to model servers and separates management traffic.

components.name: Egress proxy
components.role: Restricts outbound destinations and records approved transfers.

components.name: Tool policy adapter
components.role: Authorizes each tool operation and minimizes the data sent.

components.name: Artifact update channel
components.role: Delivers verified model and runtime updates through a controlled path.

flow.title: Map data flows
flow.description: List user requests, tool dependencies, logs, metrics, artifact downloads, and fallback routes.

flow.title: Authenticate ingress
flow.description: Require workload or user identity and enforce model and tenant access.

flow.title: Validate and admit
flow.description: Apply request size, context, and concurrency limits before inference.

flow.title: Constrain outbound work
flow.description: Authorize tool operations and route only permitted destinations through controlled egress.

flow.title: Minimize telemetry
flow.description: Export approved operational metadata without unrestricted prompt or document payloads.

flow.title: Update and audit
flow.description: Verify artifacts, rotate identities, and test that denied paths remain blocked after changes.

useCase.title: Hosting a document assistant inside a private environment
useCase.situation: A hospital administration team runs a local assistant for internal forms and operational documents.
useCase.problem: The model server is private, but a default telemetry exporter and optional remote fallback create unreviewed outbound paths.
useCase.requirement: Keep processing within the approved environment while allowing only documented enterprise integrations.
useCase.architecture: An authenticated ingress gateway fronts the service, and egress is limited to approved tool and telemetry endpoints.
runtime: An authorized staff request reaches the local model through the gateway.
A scheduling lookup passes through a tool adapter that sends only necessary identifiers.
useCase.failure: If the approved tool endpoint is unavailable, the assistant reports the missing capability instead of silently using a public fallback.
useCase.impact: Measure unauthorized connection attempts, approved data transfers, and endpoint saturation; locality is a property of the complete data flow, not model placement alone.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires maintained destination and update policies.

failures.detection: Requests lack expected identity and quota records.
failures.recovery: Restrict network reachability and require service authentication.

failures.detection: Egress denials appear after an upgrade.
failures.recovery: Review the new flow and permit only approved minimal data if required.

mistakes.fix: Inventory all outbound paths and logs.

mistakes.mistake: Using network policy as full authorization
mistakes.fix: Validate operations and data scope at the application layer.
Require an explicit approved destination and data policy.

whenToUse: Use for private or isolated model deployments.
Use where tool and telemetry destinations need control.
Use when several clients share a local inference endpoint.
whenNotToUse: Avoid exposing a raw model server to untrusted networks.
Do not rely on locality alone for confidentiality.
Avoid broad outbound access merely to simplify updates.
checklist: Inventory every network and telemetry flow.
Authorize tools independently of network rules.
Test denied egress and fallback behavior.
